decisive_items: Serum parvovirus B19 (PVB19) IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable
PVB19 DNA was found (viral load of 0.2 PVB19 DNA copies/β-globin gene copy, or 33,438 copies/μg of isolated DNA) in lesional skin biopsy specimen, but not in the serum.
an episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before first presentation
response.rationale: Direct detection of PVB19 DNA in lesional skin plus IgM/IgG serology and preceding viral prodrome strongly implicate parvovirus B19 as the cause. Normal phototesting and absence of photosensitizers/porphyrins argue against phototoxic reaction; erythema multiforme and Gianotti-Crosti lack direct lesional viral evidence and typical morphology.

rejected.why: Vesicular and vermillion lesions could suggest erythema multiforme, but no target lesions are described and PVB19 DNA in lesional skin favors direct viral infection rather than a post-infectious immune reaction.

Sun exposure and photodistribution are suggestive, but standard phototesting was unremarkable, no photosensitizer use was reported, and serum porphyrins were normal; the PVB19 evidence is otherwise unexplained.
Pruritic papules on cheeks and extremities can occur in Gianotti-Crosti syndrome, but vesicles, ear/vermillion involvement, and lesional PVB19 DNA are atypical.
